title: Muru – AI-assisted Rust server for Python apps by mod_WSGI's creator
lede: Simon Willison points to Muru, an AI-assisted Rust server for ASGI and WSGI Python apps from Graham Dumpleton, who started mod_wsgi 20 years ago.

points: Muru aims to run Python web apps well in both development and production.
Dumpleton has published about twenty posts in three weeks documenting the build as he goes, as he did with wrapture.
Topics include importing once and forking workers, HTTPS in development, canary releases, Kubernetes, scaling to zero and an in-page tracing toolbar.
In a post on AI as a lifestyle choice, he says the model does much of the visible work, but judging when something is good enough stays with him.

points.text: Commenters respect Dumpleton's mod_wsgi record but find the largely AI-written posts tedious and lifeless.
The design draws interest: preload the app, freeze the garbage collector, then fork workers, which one commenter likens to Android's Zygote.
One commenter questions why authors lean on pre-AI credentials; a reply notes the rewrite orphans a codebase built over 15 years.
A reply pushes back on a mocking reading of Dumpleton's quote, pointing to his line that AI clears the grunt work and leaves him the ideas.
